### zBuild — Vision

> The North Star for zBuild — it steers how zBuild is built. The README distills it; the wiki references it; every pipeline run is steered by it.

#### Intent
zBuild turns a delivery process into data — templates and plugins — so software is built the same disciplined way every time. We build zBuild the way zBuild builds: a minimal core, with all behavior plugin-delivered and template-composed. A good change is small, aligned to the spec, proven by a test, and wired into the live path — never scaffolding that looks finished but does nothing.

#### Principles
- **Target-agnostic by contract** — zBuild builds *any* repository, not itself; the engine and plugins never assume the target's language, layout, or that zBuild is the target. Target knowledge lives in data — templates, config, per-repo overrides — never in code.
- **Spec wins over drift** — KEEPERS, ARCHITECTURE, and the ADRs are the source of truth; when code disagrees, the code changes, not the spec.
- **Small engine, behavior at the edges** — keep the core tiny; add capability as plugins composed in templates, never by growing the engine.
- **Safety is structural** — all model-bound text passes one redaction chokepoint; state is atomic and resumable; scope is governed at every boundary.
- **Models are data, not code** — selection flows through the router and config tiers; never hardcode a model name.
- **Prove behavior, then wire it** — every change ships a test that fails without it and connects to the live path; green-but-inert is a defect.
- **Fail closed, never silent** — gates block on real problems and say why; bounded cycles and recovery drive work to done.
- **Dogfood every change** — build zBuild with zBuild; if the pipeline can't ship it, fix the pipeline.

### Rules
These are this repository's rules (.zbuild/prompts/rules.md). Work that
breaks one is wrong, whoever wrote it.

- Bash only, and match the file you are in: 4-space indent, LF line endings, a final newline, no trailing whitespace (.editorconfig). Everything must pass `shellcheck` with the repo's .shellcheckrc.
- Never pipe anything into `grep -q`, and never pipe into a bare `head`, in any `.sh` file, test files included. The reader exits early, the writer takes SIGPIPE, and under `set -o pipefail` the line fails for a reason nothing logs. Use a here-string instead: `grep -q PATTERN <<< "$var"`, or run grep on the file directly: `grep -q PATTERN "$file"`. `tests/unit/sigpipe-antipattern-guard-test.sh` fails the suite on any violation; a genuinely safe pipe is annotated `# sigpipe-ok: <reason>`.
- Never name a model (haiku, sonnet, opus, …) in code; model selection goes through core/router and config/models.json.
- A test must be able to fail: assert what is required, never what the code happens to do.
- Never edit anything under `legacy-DoNotUse/`.

#### Facts about this repo
- `ZBUILD_*` environment variables are set by the engine at dispatch (the artifact dir, the stage's input index `ZBUILD_STAGE_INPUTS`, the issue, the run). They are trusted engine inputs, not user or attacker input.
- A stage never names another stage's output — not its output name, not its file. The engine hands every stage every earlier stage's latest output, and a stage finds what it needs by what it contains (scripts/lib/earlier-output.sh; ADR-055 §1). A plugin that names another stage's output is a defect.
- Every stage writes a v2 result (`result_contract`, `verdict`, `disposition`, `reason`, detail under `data`) on every exit path, and exits 0 or 1 (ADR-054).
- `[SPEC-n]` / `[#<issue>/SPEC-n]` tags in a test tie an assertion to one issue's acceptance contract. A tag that belongs to another issue must never be changed or removed.

It is one JSON object in this shape:
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "title": "<short title>",
  "goal": "<the goal in one line>",
  "steps": [
    {"id": "step-1", "description": "<what changes and why, in one or two sentences>", "areas": ["<a directory or file the issue names>"]}

}
- `steps` is not empty; ids are "step-1", "step-2", … in order.
- Keep each item small enough to build and test on its own.
- `open_questions` holds only what the issue leaves unclear, one line each; it
  is empty when nothing is.

When the file is written, answer with one line saying how many work items it has.


## What you judge against

The issue below, in its own words.

A section of the issue that records a decision (for example "Decision:") is
binding: follow it. Anything else it proposes, such as an approach or a file
list, is a starting point: follow it unless it contradicts a decision.

If the issue has a "Definition of done", "Acceptance criteria", "Anti-patterns"
or "5-test trial" section, or a similar checklist:
1. Every Definition-of-done item is covered by at least one work item.
2. No work item does what an Anti-pattern names. If one seems to, you have

3. Do not invent permissions the issue does not grant. Nothing is "optional",

The issue:
[bug] stage timeouts silently stop applying — the fallback orchestrator ignores --timeout and a hung stage reports success

> **Rewritten 2026-10-26** against main 4bca8e94. The core of the earlier body — one whole-stage timer per dispatch in `plugin_hook_call` — has landed another way: #2394 (ADR-063, *Amendment 2026-10-15 — the engine bounds the whole stage*) added the per-stage `timeout_s:` (900 s default) and the watchdog, and #2405 / #2411 / #2414 made a stop reliable. This issue is narrowed to what is still missing. The old branch, which built a parallel `stage_timeout_s` key, was deleted unmerged. Earlier bodies are in the issue history.

Part of #1659 (engine-enforced execution bounds), under #1795 (Phase 2).

**Classification: ENGINE — `core/orch/contract.sh` × `core/pipeline/strategies/*` × `core/orch/local_engine.sh` × `core/pipeline/runner.sh` × `plugins/tool/orch-sequential/`.**

## Already done — do not rebuild

- The whole-stage limit is the template's per-stage **`timeout_s:`** (ADR-063 amendment), read by `template_stage_time_limit_v`, enforced in `plugin_hook_call` (`core/plugin-registry/lifecycle.sh`), ending `timed_out`. **No `stage_timeout_s` key, no `ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S`** — those were the earlier plan and are superseded.

## Problem (still present on main)

1. **A hung stage under `orch-sequential` reports success.** `orch-sequential` ignores `--timeout` by its own comment. `orch_load_backend` (`core/orch/contract.sh`) falls back to it when the configured backend is not found, and `_orch_load_backend` defaults to `sequential` when the config cannot be read — and discards the warning (`orch_load_backend "$backend" 2>/dev/null || true`). No `backend.degraded` event is emitted.
2. **A flat 300 s collect deadline undercuts the stage's own limit.** `_strategy_run_map` (`map.sh`), `_fanout` (`fanout.sh`) and `_sequential` (`sequential.sh`) pass `orch_collect --timeout "${ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT:-300}"` — a stage whose `timeout_s:` is longer than 300 s is cut off at 300 s on the orchestrator route.
3. **`router.timeout_s` still means two things.** `_runner_dispatch_always_run` (`core/pipeline/runner.sh`) reads the stage's `router.timeout_s` (fallback `ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT:-30`) as the whole-stage bound for the teardown stages; everywhere else it bounds one model call.
4. **Killing is still hand-rolled in two places.** The `always_run` watchdog in `_runner_dispatch_always_run` does its own TERM → 2 s → KILL on the group; `core/orch/local_engine.sh` has `_orch_local_kill_slot` with 0.5 s waits. `zbuild_pg_kill` (`scripts/lib/proc-group.sh`) is the shared helper.

## Decisions

1. **`orch-sequential` is retired.** Delete `plugins/tool/orch-sequential/` and its golden; remove the built-in lookup and both fallbacks in `orch_load_backend`; a config naming `sequential` / `orch-sequential` is unknown like any other. Tests using it as a fixture move to `orch-mock` (or `bash-parallel` where real process behaviour is the point); tests of the plugin itself are deleted. The **`sequential` strategy** (`_strategy_run_sequential`, template `strategy: sequential`) is a different thing and stays.
2. **A missing or unreadable backend is a hard error** — `misconfigured`, naming the backend. No silent fallback, no discarded warning.
3. **No flat backend limit.** The strategies stop passing `ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT`; the stage's `timeout_s:` (enforced in `plugin_hook_call`) is the only stage limit.
4. **`router.timeout_s` bounds one model call, nothing else.** The `always_run` stages are bounded by their `timeout_s:` like every other stage, keeping their current values (release 30 s, persist 120 s), set in the shipped templates.
5. **Kill through `zbuild_pg_kill`.** The `always_run` watchdog and `_orch_local_kill_slot` use it; no hand-rolled TERM/KILL sequence remains for stage dispatch.

## Not in scope

- With **no** config file at all, the default backend (`bash-parallel`) is used, as today — that is not `misconfigured`.
- Which backends a test runs under, and how fixture tests are migrated off `orch-sequential` (decision 1) — those are build's choices, checked by the full suite (`npm test`).

- A whole-run lifetime limit — #1944.
- Changing the per-stage `timeout_s:` mechanism, its default, or its values (ADR-063 amendment).
- Changing how fan-out or the cycle/retry loop work.

## ADR

- **ADR-011 — amended:** `orch-sequential` is retired; the default backend is `bash-parallel`; a missing or unreadable backend is `misconfigured`, not a fallback (supersedes graceful-degradation rule 2 for the orchestrator); strategies pass no collect timeout.
- **ADR-017 — amended:** `router.timeout_s` bounds one model call only; `always_run` stages are bounded by `timeout_s:` (ADR-063 amendment).
- Each amended statement names its test in an `## Enforced by` entry (CLAUDE.md, #2268).

## Acceptance

- [ ] A hung `run` hook dispatched through the **orchestrator route** (map, fanout, sequential strategy) is stopped at its stage's `timeout_s:` and ends `timed_out` naming the stage and the limit.
- [ ] A stage whose `timeout_s:` is above 300 s and which runs longer than 300 s on the orchestrator route completes; `ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT` is no longer read.
- [ ] `orch-sequential` is gone: plugin dir and `tests/golden/orch-sequential-capabilities.golden` deleted, and no file outside `docs/adr/` names `orch-sequential` (a guard test enforces it); a config naming `sequential` or `orch-sequential` ends `misconfigured`.
- [ ] A configured backend that cannot be found, or a config file that exists but cannot be read or parsed, fails the run as `misconfigured` naming the backend — tested from the **installed** tree (`install.sh` layout), not only the checkout.
- [ ] `release` / `persist` are bounded by `timeout_s:` (30 s / 120 s); `_runner_dispatch_always_run` no longer reads `router.timeout_s`.
- [ ] The `always_run` watchdog and `_orch_local_kill_slot` kill through `zbuild_pg_kill`; a hook that spawns a child which ignores TERM leaves nothing running.
- [ ] Before writing tests: `grep -rl` for `orch-sequential`, `ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT`, `ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT`, `router.timeout_s` and `_orch_local_kill_slot` in `tests/` — every test that pins them is in scope (CLAUDE.md, test scope discovery).
- [ ] ADR-011 and ADR-017 amended with `## Enforced by` entries.
- [ ] `npm test` + `npm run lint` green.

Refs #1659, #1944, #2394, #2405, #2411, #2414, ADR-063 (amendment 2026-10-15), ADR-054 §6a, ADR-017, ADR-011, #2333.

# Plan notes — issue #1801

## Reading the issue

Issue: stage timeouts silently stop applying — fallback orchestrator ignores --timeout, hung stage reports success.

### Already done (do not rebuild)
- Whole-stage `timeout_s:` per stage in templates (ADR-063 amendment), enforced in `plugin_hook_call` via lifecycle.sh watchdog.
- `stage_timeout_s` / `ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S` superseded — do not touch.

### Problems still present
1. `orch-sequential` ignores `--timeout`; `orch_load_backend` silently falls back to it when backend not found; `_orch_load_backend` defaults to sequential when config unreadable, discards warning. No `backend.degraded` event.
2. Strategies (`_strategy_run_map`, `_fanout`, `_sequential`) pass `orch_collect --timeout "${ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT:-300}"` — cuts off stages whose `timeout_s:` is > 300 s.
3. `_runner_dispatch_always_run` reads `router.timeout_s` (fallback `ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT:-30`) as a whole-stage bound for teardown stages — wrong; should use `timeout_s:`.
4. Hand-rolled TERM→2s→KILL in `_runner_dispatch_always_run`; hand-rolled TERM/0.5s/KILL in `_orch_local_kill_slot`; `zbuild_pg_kill` exists as shared helper and should be used.

### Decisions (binding)
1. `orch-sequential` is retired — plugin dir + golden deleted; no built-in lookup; sequential/orch-sequential treated as unknown.
2. Missing or unreadable backend → `misconfigured` hard error naming backend. No fallback.
3. No flat collect deadline — strategies drop `ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT`; `timeout_s:` is the only limit.
4. `router.timeout_s` bounds one model call only. `always_run` stages use `timeout_s:` (30s/120s in shipped templates).
5. Kill via `zbuild_pg_kill` in both places.

## Plan structure: 15 steps

Original 13 steps, updated for test-stage open findings, plus 2 new steps; updated again for design-stage findings.

### Changes from prior plan

**Step 3 modified**: Add `.github/issues/keepers-manifest.yaml` to areas — the guard test named it as still
referencing orch-sequential. Also `tests/integration/orch-backend-misconfigured-test.sh` (a new
test file) contains an orch-sequential reference and must be cleaned.

**Step 6 modified**: The test must check timed_out propagation for all three strategies (map, fanout,
sequential-strategy), not only fanout — test-author finding 1. The variable that must be checked is
`_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME` from the collect call.

**Step 7 modified (test stage)**: The strategy implementation must set `_ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME=timed_out` (not
`failed`) when the collect call returns a timed_out outcome via `_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME`. The test
failure message was: "got '<empty>'; old code passes collect_rc=1 → _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME=failed" —
meaning the implementation maps collect_rc=1 to failed, but must read _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME first.

**Step 8 modified**: The test must separately verify release at 30s AND persist at 120s as two hung-
stage scenarios — test-author finding 2.

**Step 9 modified**: The runner regression shows the always_run dispatch changes broke pre-existing
tests (`always-run-exit-paths-test.sh` SPEC-5: a 60s release hook held the exit; `runner-release-
exit-paths-test.sh` SPEC-5: cleanup not dispatched). The fix must correctly route always_run dispatch
to use timeout_s: without breaking the dispatch of cleanup stages for prior pipeline stages.

**Step 2 modified**: Deleting `orch-sequential-test.sh` must be confirmed safe by checking whether
the behaviors it asserted are now covered by other tests — test-author finding 3.

**NEW step 13**: Fix `set -e` mid-file lint violations in `orch-timeout-applies-test.sh`
(8 occurrences), `orch-backend-misconfigured-test.sh` (2 occurrences), and
`orch-kill-uses-pg-kill-guard-test.sh` (1 occurrence) — replace with `cmd || rc=$?` pattern.

**NEW step 14**: Fix the `core/pipeline/runner.sh` regression that broke 14+ integration tests
(happy path exits 0; always-run dispatch; cleanup dispatch; pipeline.end not emitted; stage manifests
contract broken). These all trace to the step 9 build changes to runner.sh.

**Old step 13** (npm test + lint green) becomes **step 15**.

### Changes from design stage

**Step 3 modified (design)**: SPEC-11 requires adding a NEW pool isolation assertion tagged
`[#1801/SPEC-11]` to `plugins/tool/orch-mock/tests/orch-mock-test.sh` (not just migrating existing
tests). SPEC-12 requires updating 5 additional test files that iterate or assert on orch-sequential
behavior: `tests/unit/adr059-no-tmpdir-defaults-test.sh`, `tests/unit/core-orch-run-id-isolation-test.sh`,
`tests/unit/dispatch-rc-guard-test.sh`, `tests/unit/stdin-spawn-guard-test.sh`,
`tests/unit/summary-mandatory-test.sh`. These are now added to step-3's areas and description.
Two golden event-sequence files added to areas in case pipeline-event changes from deletion land there.

**Step 7 modified (design)**: Original plan said "remove ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT argument from collect
calls." Design requires REPLACING it with `template_stage_time_limit "$stage"`. Simply removing the
argument would prevent `orch_collect` from ever emitting `_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME=timed_out`, breaking
SPEC-1. The stage's declared timeout_s: (default 900 s) is passed instead of the flat 300 s cap.
`scripts/lib/stage-time-limit.sh` added to step-7's areas since strategies must source it.

**Step 9 modified (design)**: `tests/unit/exit-path-teardown-budget-guard-test.sh` added to areas.
Its SPEC-1 and SPEC-3 assertions grep for the variable renamed from `ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT` to
`_SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT` in `runner-release-exit-paths-test.sh`; without updating the guard test,
the budget guard breaks on the rename. The step-9 description now names this update explicitly.

None.
